**Construct Dual Grid:** Map each cell center of the AMR grid to a vertex in the dual grid.
**Extract Isosurface:** Apply the standard Marching Cubes algorithm (as defined in [Grid Structure and Topology](14934-grid-structure-and-topology.md)) on the dual grid vertices.
**Stitching (if required):** If the gap between coarse and fine grids results in uncovered regions, a tessellation scheme (stitch cells) is used to merge the levels seamlessly.
This is handled by the variant [Dual Grid Isosurface Extraction with Stitch Cells](10500-dual-grid-isosurface-extraction-with-stitch-cells.md).
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of voxels in the dual grid, similar to standard Marching Cubes.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of cell centers in the AMR data.
*   **Strengths:** Eliminates cracks caused by dangling nodes in AMR data without requiring complex post-processing or interpolation artifacts.
*   **Limitations:** Requires a stitching mechanism (like stitch cells) to handle the geometric gaps between coarse and fine levels if a continuous mesh across levels is needed.
*   **When to use:** When extracting isosurfaces from AMR data where standard vertex-centered resampling leads to topological errors.
The method was introduced to address issues in extracting isosurfaces from Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) data.
